title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Page context for open tabs in the Copilot desktop app built-in browser
summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot desktop app will use content from open tabs in its built-in browser as page context for answering questions and summaries, scoped to the current conversation. Rolling out worldwide mid to late November 2026. No action required; verify browser enablement and governance settings.
body:
[What and why]

Copilot in the desktop app will be able to use content from open webpage tabs in the app's built-in browser as page context. Users will be able to ask questions or request summaries for a single tab or across multiple tabs, which helps with multi-tab workflows. Page context will be scoped to the current conversation and will apply only when the built-in browser is enabled. 

Availability is limited to the Microsoft Copilot desktop app.

[Rollout schedule]

- General availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete the rollout in late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users of the Copilot desktop app in organizations where the built-in browser is enabled- Admins who manage the Copilot desktop app and its built-in browserPlatforms and services

- Copilot desktop app (built-in browser)- Microsoft 365 CopilotWhat will happen

- When the built-in browser is enabled, Copilot will be able to use content from open webpage tabs in that browser to answer questions and provide summaries: 

- Users will be able to ask about a single tab or across multiple tabs: 

- Page context will be limited to the current conversation.- If the built-in browser is disabled, this feature will not be active and will have no impact.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

- Confirm whether the Copilot desktop app built-in browser is enabled for your organization.- Review the governance settings for in-app browsing and page context use.- Validate the expected behavior with pilot users.- Tell users and helpdesk staff that page context is limited to the current conversation.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswerDoes the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Copilot uses content from open webpage tabs in the built-in browser as context for answers and summaries.Does the change give users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can ask questions or request summaries for one tab or across multiple tabs.
